html:
Colonia del Sacramento is a town on the Río de la Plata in Uruguay, founded by the Portuguese in 1680 opposite Buenos Aires. Its old quarter is a World Heritage Site.

Portugal built it to push the border of Brazil south to the great river and to smuggle goods into Spanish lands. Spain attacked it again and again, and the town changed hands several times by war and treaty until Spain kept it in 1777. Its narrow streets mix Portuguese and Spanish building.

The struggle over Colonia led Spain to found Montevideo as a counterweight. The east bank of the river, the Banda Oriental, stayed contested between the two empires and their heirs, until the Cisplatine War made Uruguay a separate country.
sum: Colonia del Sacramento is a town on the Río de la Plata in Uruguay, founded by the Portuguese in 1680 opposite Buenos Aires. Its old quarter is a World Heritage Site.
